_: THE ONE LIST BOTH PLANES ARE TESTED AGAINST (#1389).
`rich_text` is the only field type whose stored value is markup, and the
rule for whether one is EMPTY therefore cannot be a trim: richtext.Sanitize

strips no empty elements, so


survives it, trims to itself, and
would pass a required check while rendering as nothing at all.
So there is ONE rule with two implementations, one per language:
app/internal/richtext.IsEmpty   (server-authoritative, refuses the write)
web/src/lib/fieldDisplay.ts     (isFieldValueEmpty / htmlToPlainText,
which the field count and the editor's
Set-versus-Clear decision are built on)
Two implementations of one rule drift. This file is what stops them: both
suites READ IT rather than carrying their own copy of the case list, so a
change that moves one plane and not the other fails on the other plane's
test rather than being noticed by somebody looking at a blank field.
`stored` is MEASURED, not asserted from memory: it is what richtext.Sanitize

actually produced for `input`. Note

 

, whose entity reaches
storage as a literal U+00A0 — which is why neither predicate may be written
against the entity string.
Read by app/internal/richtext/richtext_test.go and
web/src/lib/fieldDisplay.test.ts. If you add a case here, both pick it up.
